chapter: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
title: Meeting Buster Smith in Dallas and the Texas music school
summary: He met Buster Smith in Dallas while at a music school under Professor Barnett, played dances with his band, and calls Smith self-taught and the greatest.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, where had you met Buster Smith?
Dallas, Texas.
Yeah? What were you doing there when you met him?
I was living in Terro, going to school 30 miles.
Oh.
It was a musical school, see.
Oh, so you -- this is another --
That was a musical school. They had a

teacher there named Professor Barnett, and it was one of them schools out there where the principal, anything he wanted to do, the whites backed it. So he had school, he had everything going on in that school.
Oh, yeah?

All kind of -- he had the best band in Texas in that school there. And the best of the musicians came out of that band. And so I was always active with the music. So I used to go to Dallas, 32 miles, go over there on Sundays with a girl and ride, you know, things like that. And that's how I met Buster Smith and I started playing with him. We played dances with some of the little groups, even with Buster's little band.
Now, Buster had a band, did he?
Yeah, he had a band, too, had a little band there.
Well, now, he was a well-schooled musician.
To me, he was the greatest.
Well, where did he get this stuff from? I mean, how --
Himself.
Huh?
I think he was self-taught.
Self-taught?
Yeah, like Herschel.
Oh, I wondered, because he always sounded --
He writes a lot now.
Yeah, but it sounded as thought he were a little better schooled than the average guy.
Yeah, yeah. Well, he got into it later, and you can teach yourself from books and --
Yeah, of course, yeah.
-- experience.
But not everybody has that kind of mind, where you go and buy books or get books.
